notes.title: Dev Talk - Q&A
notes.content:
[h3]Dear Survivors, this is NAKWON Governing Committee.[/h3]

This Q&A list was written based on your questions on Discord.
Visit our [url=https://discord.gg/nakwon]official Discord[/url] and join the discussion.

[h3]Q. I have questions about the game UI.[/h3]
Please inform us about the UI placement, whether it will be minimized like EFT or not.
Such as the HP, stamina, weapon types and durability costs.

[b]A. [/b]Currently, we are planning to show all essential information the player needs to survive.
However, we will hide or replace other elements that might spoil the gameplay.
e.g.: HP, stamina, and all available means with an immediate impact on survival will be shown. 
But other elements that can be replaced by being displayed in another way such as a mini map, will not be included.


[h3]Q. I have questions about the item preservation.[/h3]
Will there be any insurance feature that allows you to get back the items even if you die, such as a secure container like EFT?

[b]A. [/b]First, there will be no insurance system in the pre-alpha version. It means, you would lose everything you took with you if you died during scouting.
However, this is not the final specification. 
We will keep on considering additional developments based on the user experience during pre-alpha session and the direction that suits our gameplay.
The system in EFT that you mentioned might be a reference for us during the development process. 
But we want to avoid adding a definite method to obtain resources every time without having to lose anything.


[h3]Q. I have questions about scouting.[/h3]
“All citizens must join scouting regularly. It is possible to rest without scouting, but the number of Scouts that one may skip differs according to the Citizen Grade.” - from the scouting Guide for Novice Survivor.
Will I get some kind of penalty if I exceed the number of ‘rests’ allowed? (e.g., citizen class demotion, fines, etc.)
I want to know if real-time will be applied in the game (so scouting will be a daily mission) or will there be any other concepts of time in the game.

[b]A. [/b]Here is the answer for your questions about scouting and concept of time in the game.
First, below is an explanation of the concept of time.
[list]
[*] Concepts of time: 
It won’t be related to real-time. Each player will have their own ‘date’ in the game.
It will not flow in real-time, and it will only flow every time you do any act of spending the day.
[/list] Currently, there are two activities available for players to spend a day.
[olist]
[*] Scouting: One day will pass after scouting.
[*] Sleep: One day will pass upon sleeping.
[/olist] By choosing to sleep, you will pass a day, which can be used to recover an injury (e.g., broken ankle cures after 3 days, etc.) or other things that needs recovery too.
But your Fullness will decrease each day and food intake is required.
[list]
[*] Number of scouting: 
To prevent the act of only sleeping by saving a large pile of food,
we made a rule where you are allowed to do other activities without scouting for certain number of days, after you completed one scouting.
[/list] However, this feature may not be added in pre-alpha version.


[h3]Q. I have questions about secondary creation (fan creation).[/h3]
Can I make any fan creation such as fan fiction or fan art based on the revealed story and information of NAKWON and post it in this Discord server or any other communities?
I will identify the source and will not use it for commercial purposes.

[b]A. [/b]About this one, we will need time to discuss about it internally since this has not been discussed yet.
However, I personally doubt whether if any fan creation would be meaningful for the time being since we have yet to reveal all information and worldview, or let you experience the game properly.
Also, due to the worldview and story of NAKWON is rarely include in pre-alpha version, I think it would be better for fan creations to be made after the game is further developed with more organized worldview/information.


[h3]Q: I have questions regarding future plans related to rent, commission, consumption, and server wipe/reset?[/h3]
In EFT and Rust, since goods or supplies are piled up excessively, they reset the progress every six months.
I want to know if there will be server wipe/reset system.
Since if you are going to add server wipe, a lot of central systems would be necessary.
E.g.: If the rent is not paid, NAKWON's base facility will be locked and unavailable, or players will be kicked out from the base with a box filled with their items.
In any case, I wish there will be a balanced system in goods consumption.
For long-term returning players who got overdue rent and locked base, I think they should get some kind of protection.
Also, the durability and maintenance of the base could help in the continuous consumption of goods and items.
Such as aging facilities where pipes get old, so players would need new pipes or duck tapes.

[b]A: [/b]Here is the answer about the direction of the housing and server wipe.
[list]
[*] Server wipe: 
The cycle of resources acquisition/consumption is critical in games where players can preserve and accumulate resources.
Since the motivation will get weaker as the time goes, if resources accumulate indefinitely.
Therefore, many of the Loot-Escape genres, including EFT, provide the motivation to play by periodically wiping players' resources.
However, I think there are many cases where you feel progressing the game is meaningless due to the forced wipe and results in quitting the game.
So we're approaching in a way that material assets should not be wiped, and we are trying to create lots of cases where players may choose to consume resources for gameplay progress. We are trying to make sure consuming resources to be reasonable and provide benefits accordingly.
[/list][list]
[*] Housing: 
I'm thinking of housing as one of the consumption factors of resources.
We are considering a structure where each player can choose the type of accommodation they can stay for a certain period of time, so that they can endure the benefits/cost of housing according to their own choice.
Therefore, players will need to choose whether to stay in an accommodation where rent is free with only minimal function or an accommodation with many benefits and functions but expensive rent has to be paid up front.
This way, players will need to consume and collect resources during the process.
It's very similar to your concept that the base facility will be locked and unusable if the rent is not paid, with all their items being put in a box.
If you are in a good accommodation where you can place a lot of furniture and then moved to a cheap accommodation because you cannot afford the rent, you won't be able to place all your existing furniture which means you won't be able to activate some of the effects.
However, even if you didn't login to the game for a long time, you won't be behind on your rent.
This game has nothing to do with real time and time will not pass if the player didn't act.
The goal is to make sure that everyone can enjoy the game either for a short time or long time without the pressure of time attack. [/list]

[h3]Q. I have questions about poisonous gas.[/h3]
I want to know the purpose of poisonous gas.
If it's a time limit during a game session, I want to know when the poisonous gas spreads.

[b]A. [/b]The role of poisonous gas is the time limit.
We had various ideas to create a time limit until the escape. We conclude that pushing players out of the map by spreading poisonous gas is more suitable to our game instead of just a plain countdown clock.
If there was a countdown clock, players may feel anxiety throughout the game keep thinking about 'when' they should depart to the exit to make it on time. 
Due to the nature of the game, you will need enough time to move and reach the destination. 
But often, it's impossible to arrive at the exit using the rest of the time depending on the situation.
So, we visualized the time limit into a form of poisonous gas, inducing a natural escape by slowly pushing players from a random position at the end of the map each time.
Since we want this to work as a concept of the time limit, we have balanced this poisonous gas to spread slowly enough so you will have time to farm items. 
At the beginning of the scavenge session, you will be informed which direction the gas will spread. Poisonous gas will start spreading very slowly which will get a little faster towards the end. 
After 25 minutes, the poisonous gas will cover the whole map. It will be balanced through tests.


[h3]Q. I have questions about the communication system.[/h3]
Can players use voice chat? If voice chat is available, I want to know how much it will affect the zombies since they are sound-sensitive.
How about emotes? An emote system would be great for some players who don't want to use voice/text chat during gameplay.
Also, when selling items at the trading center, will it be a simple way to register items for sale?
Or will it be the same as real-life trading, by writing a post describing an item for sale and contacting the buyers directly for a transaction?

[b]A. [/b]Here is the answer to your questions.
[list]
[*]  Communication system: 
No related features have been implemented in the pre-alpha version. 
We are still considering adding voice chat, but we haven't discussed this in depth.
Also, 'voice chats affecting zombies' is certainly interesting but on the other hand, we are worried that it could be too stressful and being abused. We are going to discuss regarding voice chat after the pre-alpha session.
Also, we don't intend to include text chat during scavenging, which means there won't be emotes either.
Instead, we are thinking of adding body movements to communicate. However, it is not confirmed because we have not discussed this in depth either.
[*] Trading center: 
This is scheduled to be developed after the pre-alpha session so the direction has not been confirmed yet. 
However, I have been thinking of applying an easy way so many players can use it comfortably (registration/search/transaction for sale, etc.). 
Even though it would be more realistic if you do the transaction directly, I think the discomfort will increase as you play.
The trading center will be developed after pre-alpha, so the possibility of a change in direction is always open.
[/list]

[h3]Q. Will it support Xbox Controller, DualSense/Shock, Pro-Controller, and SteamDeck interface in the future?[/h3]

[b]A. [/b]Here is the answer to your question regarding the support of various devices.
[list]
[*] Console: Unfortunately, we don't have enough time to support this in the pre-alpha session. 
Also, since we need to develop the game even more after the pre-alpha, it's difficult to answer when it will be supported. 
However, since the UI was designed in consideration of consoles from the beginning, there is a possibility that consoles will be supported if the circumstances allow.
[*] SteamDeck: Same as above. It is currently not supported.
[/list]

[h3]Q. I have questions about growth factors in the game.[/h3]
Since this is a survival game, I believe there are some factors that will change with time as the player progress.
I want to know whether if the character growth will be same as RPG games, where players can choose which one to master upon leveling up, or will the character naturally improves based on the activities done, or will there be a different/new method.

[b]A. [/b]We haven't discussed this in depth, but our goal is to make growth factors to not feel unreasonable/unfair. 
I think it's closer to the former since some players who are not good in activities wouldn't be able to grow in the latter case. 
We want to make sure players have chances to grow even if they don't have skills.
We are going to discuss this in depth in the future.


[h3]Q. I have questions about body parts HP and penalty due to injury.[/h3]
Are you going to add body parts HP and debuffs depending on injury severity, like EFT?

[b]A. [/b]There will be only one HP bar, but injury may occur at different body parts.
Currently, we don't have plans for HP for different body parts, but we are considering condition abnormalities caused by the injury at each body part (e.g., damage on the leg caused leg fracture debuff)
However, body part condition abnormalities have not been developed yet for pre-alpha.


[h3]Q. I have questions regarding stats and abnormal condition types.[/h3]
There are lots of different abnormal condition types in survival games such as DayZ, EFT, Don't Starve, and This War of Mine. EFT has the most types.
I want to know how many stats and abnormal condition types will there be for NAKWON.

[b]A. [/b]Our goal is to make the game easy to understand in the beginning. So available stat are Fullness, HP, and Stamina.
However, we are planning to add more abnormal condition effects in buffs and debuffs form in the future so that you can experience various situations.
Abnormal condition (example): Hunger, fracture, exhaustion, cold, flu, etc
Hunger stat will be available in pre-alpha session.


[h3]Q. I have questions regarding the cost of this game.[/h3]
Do I need to buy this game, or can I play this game for free?
If I have to buy this game, I want to know how much will it cost to purchase the game.

[b]A. [/b]So far, we are considering this game to be free to play with BM, such as battle pass. It's a bit different from the past, so I think players would be reluctant to play if they need to pay to play the game. 
However, this is not confirmed yet.
Either way, there won't be any pay-to-win element in this game. We hope many people will enjoy this game.

Also, we don't intend to include text chat during scavenging, which means there won't be emotes either.
Instead, we are thinking of adding body movements to communicate.
However, it is not confirmed because we have not discussed this in depth either.

Trading center: 
This is scheduled to be developed after the pre-alpha session so the direction has not been confirmed yet.
However, I have been thinking of applying an easy way so many players can use it comfortably (registration/search/transaction for sale, etc.).
Even though it would be more realistic if you do the transaction directly, I think the discomfort will increase as you play.
The trading center will be developed after pre-alpha, so the possibility of a change in direction is always open.
Console: Unfortunately, we don't have enough time to support this in the pre-alpha session.
Also, since we need to develop the game even more after the pre-alpha, it's difficult to answer when it will be supported.
However, since the UI was designed in consideration of consoles from the beginning, there is a possibility that consoles will be supported if the circumstances allow.
SteamDeck: Same as above.
It is currently not supported.
We haven't discussed this in depth, but our goal is to make growth factors to not feel unreasonable/unfair.
I think it's closer to the former since some players who are not good in activities wouldn't be able to grow in the latter case.
We want to make sure players have chances to grow even if they don't have skills.
We are going to discuss this in depth in the future.
There will be only one HP bar, but injury may occur at different body parts.

Currently, we don't have plans for HP for different body parts, but we are considering condition abnormalities caused by the injury at each body part (e.g., damage on the leg caused leg fracture debuff)
However, body part condition abnormalities have not been developed yet for pre-alpha.
Our goal is to make the game easy to understand in the beginning.
So available stat are Fullness, HP, and Stamina.
However, we are planning to add more abnormal condition effects in buffs and debuffs form in the future so that you can experience various situations.
Abnormal condition (example): Hunger, fracture, exhaustion, cold, flu, etc
Hunger stat will be available in pre-alpha session.
So far, we are considering this game to be free to play with BM, such as battle pass.
It's a bit different from the past, so I think players would be reluctant to play if they need to pay to play the game.
However, this is not confirmed yet.
Either way, there won't be any pay-to-win element in this game.
We hope many people will enjoy this game.

notes.title: Dev Talk - Q&A
notes.content:
[h3]Dear Survivors, this is NAKWON's Game Director Jang Kyoung Han.[/h3]

Thank you for your interest in NAKWON: LAST PARADISE.
This Q&A list was written based on your questions as seen below.



[h3]Q. How do I join the pre-alpha tests?[/h3]
[b]A. [/b]We are planning to make the pre-alpha test open to anyone with Steam. 
We will announce the details soon.



[h3]Q. Is the pre-alpha test completely confidential, or is it allowed to be discussed in live broadcasts or YouTube videos?[/h3]
[b]A. [/b]As we are planning for the test to be open to anyone on Steam, please feel free to share content of the game. 
We always welcome live streams.



[h3]Q. When is the game’s release?[/h3]
[b]A. [/b]As for the actual release/launch of the game, it will take some time. 
The pre-alpha test will be within this year, and details will be announced through official community channels.



[h3]Q. For the pre-alpha test, would a selected pool of people gain access to it or is it an ‘early access’ open to anyone on Steam?[/h3]
[b]A. [/b]We are thinking of a test where anyone can try playing through Steam for a certain period. 
It would be different from early access or launch.



[h3]Q. What area does the game’s map cover? Are there any plans to expand the map range?[/h3]
[b]A. [/b]Currently, we have implemented gameplay within an area roughly equivalent to one block around Jongno 3-ga subway station. 
We plan to continue expanding from this central location. 
We will dive deeper into this subject on the fifth week of #dev-talk [url=https://discord.gg/nakwon]in the official Discord server[/url], where we will discuss ‘game content(levels)’.



[h3]Q. What direction is the BM headed? [/h3]
[b]A. [/b]Of course we are excluding Pay-to-Win elements as P2W is not a good fit with this game, but we are considering a Battle Pass-centered BM, including emotes and costumes. 
We haven’t given this particular area too much thought yet. 



[h3]Q. I'm curious if NAKWON will operate on periodical resets or seasons like similar games.[/h3]
[b]A. [/b]We plan to have seasonal updates, but we are not considering asset resets. 
Instead, we are thinking of resetting season ranks or achievements. 

Some may wonder if inflation would become an issue if we do not implement asset resets, but we believe this could be resolved by making resources continuously consumed in the NAKWON Safety Zone. 
Food will be needed every day to survive, and depending on where in the Safety Zone you live, survivors will need to pay rent. 

The top players may be required to send ‘donations’ to the NAKWON Safety Zone, and we are also thinking of creating a high-level Scouting mode only available to those users.



[h3]Q. Will the pre-alpha test showcase any ‘Simulation’ content?[/h3]
[b]A. [/b]Only the minimum. 
Our current objective is to complete developing the food system, Citizen Grades, unlocking city areas, Store system and random event systems before the test. 

Housing, Quests, achievements, ranking and Citizen Market are under consideration. These features are to be updated after the test and are subject to change.



[h3]Q. Is NAKWON a co-op game?[/h3]
[b]A. [/b]For the pre-alpha test, we plan to develop two types of parties (solo, duo). 
If you want to scout the city alone, you can do it solo, and if you want to scout the city with a friend, you can party up with a friend and move in duos. 
While you're in the city, you may encounter other solo or duo players.



[h3]Q. Is there an ETA on the pre-alpha test? I'm very ready to get into it.[/h3]
[b]A. [/b]Thank you for the support. 
We know a lot of people are eager to try NAKWON, and we definitely want to share our project with you as well. 
The test will take place this year, and the ETA will be announced in a month or two.



[h3]Q. Will it be available to create private servers online, and will the game be open to users creating various user mods?[/h3]
[b]A. [/b]As we are thinking of an MMO environment(economy including Citizen Market, ranking, etc) encompassing all users, private servers are more likely to be unavailable. 
As for game mods, it is too soon to consider as the game is still at its very early stages and resources are limited.



[h3]Q. Like ‘Escape from Tarkov’, which is of similar genre, does the health system vary depending on how damaged each body part is, or would it be a unified health system like in FPS games?[/h3]
[b]A. [/b]In NAKWON, injuries are not managed separately for each body part. 

However, the damage you take will vary depending on which body part was attacked. 
Whether the attack comes from the front or back (for example, suddenly being attacked from behind) will also affect the damage received. 
Armor equipped on specific body parts can absorb damage directed at that area until the armor is broken. 

Injuries and conditions based on body parts will be managed in the form of debuffs. For example, if you fall from a height, there's a chance of a 'leg injury' condition occurring, which would slow down your movement speed.



[h3]Q. Wouldn’t it be easier to create a more frightening atmosphere if the zombies reacted to the flashlight?[/h3]
[b]A. [/b]That is a great idea, but while we agree that it would definitely be more scary, we thought the game would be less fun if it becomes too difficult to play. 
Also, it would be hard to tell if the zombies are reacting to the light, or because they saw the player. This is why we decided on the current way where zombies react more to sound.



[h3]Q. Besides the normal zombies, will there be boss zombie types which are huntable but still more difficult to fight against?[/h3]
[b]A. [/b]Currently we don’t have any plans for more difficult zombies, as we don’t want to make hunting zombies the main objective.



[h3]Q. How do you plan to motivate survivors to farm, and how do you intend to stimulate the in-game economy?[/h3]
[b]A. [/b]This is actually one of the most vital points in farming-escape genre games like Tarkov. 
Once the motivation for farming disappears, and the penalties for losing assets due to death become insignificant, the overall tension in the game diminishes. 

Therefore, we plan to allocate a significant amount of effort to the structure of motivation for farming and its sustainability within the game.
In summary, we are considering a survival ‘Simulation’ format where players continue the game by surviving day by day. 
Each day, they have the option to perform one of several actions, including Scouting (actual gameplay). 
During this process, the following elements will constantly consume resources:
[list]
[*] Fullness: Decreases by a certain amount every day. Farming and consuming food are necessary to satisfy it.
[*] Random Events: These events occur randomly as each day passes. Depending on the choices made, they can lead to changes in your assets. For example, if you encounter a theft, your decision to pursue or give up can result in different outcomes.
[/list]

Apart from the mentioned elements above, through housing and different elements, we plan to require daily maintenance fees to keep the following aspects in better condition:
[list]
[*] Maintaining Survival-Enhancing Buffs: You can activate certain characteristics through furniture placement in housing that helps with survival. However, a higher housing rent may be required as multiple furniture placement slots are needed.
[*] Reduced Risks: Placing appliances like refrigerators in your accommodation can increase the shelf life of food. However, accommodations that require electricity can come with higher rent.
[/list]

If you ask what would be the characteristics that help survival, while there are offensive elements, mobility, parkour skills, stamina management, and jumping abilities all come in to play.

As these details are still under development, they are not finalized and may change, but we trust that you get the idea of how we are planning to go about this topic.
Only a very minimum of this ‘Simulation’ will be shown in the pre-alpha test. 

In this test, we are more focused on Scouting, which is a different approach to the zombie game genre.
Besides the benefits that come from certain aspects in ‘Simulation’, we are planning to delve deeper into gear and detailed options in the future. Here’s a list of what we are thinking of now, which of course can be changed.
[list]
[*] Detailed Gear Options: As in Diablo
[*] Melee Weapon Customization: Detailed parts for each type of melee weapon and customization features
[*] Diversification of Gadgets (Gloves, Shoes): Ice-cleat shoes, lightweight shoes for increased speed, gloves for improved parkour, gloves for climbing pipes, etc
[*] Various Accessories: A variety of accessories, such as devices that audibly alert you of moving objects in your vicinity or wristwatches that constantly display a mini-map
[/list]


[h3]Q. Do you have any plans to develop vehicles to ride like cars?[/h3]
[b]A. [/b]Currently there are no plans as it clashes with the game’s purpose.



[h3]Q. What is the method for collecting rare items (e.g., extremely rare items apart from RPG-style collectibles)? Will it be through exploring hidden areas or probability-based drops?[/h3]
[b]A. [/b]Depending on the item, we plan to distribute it through various channels, and we are looking forward to seeing players discover these on their own while scouting.



[h3]Q. I'm curious if there are any measures in place for bankruptcy. New players may struggle to deal with zombies or escaping, and it's possible for them to lose all their assets until it becomes zero. What happens in such cases?[/h3]
[b]A. [/b]Every time a player dies, we plan to provide minimum items (e.g., a piece of lumber) for Scouting, so there won't be a situation where the game becomes unplayable due to having zero assets. 

Costs like housing rent will be paid in advance for seven days, so bankruptcy won't have an immediate impact. 
Additionally, we intend to set probabilities for random events that act as relief measures based on the player's asset situation. 

Asset-zero situations are more likely to occur in the early stages of the game.



[h3]Q. Can we visit a friend’s accommodation?[/h3]
[b]A. [/b]As accommodations do not exist physically (they only exist as UI slots), visiting a friend’s accommodation would not be possible. (Though that would be a cool idea.)



[h3]Q. If it's impossible to completely kill zombies, will there be weapons or items that can incapacitate them on a wide scale or put them in a groggy-like state with one hit? [/h3]
[b]A. [/b]Shotguns are planned to serve that role. 

Also, it seems that many people are concerned with the fact that the zombies cannot be killed, but the balance of combat with zombies is being approached like dealing with basic mobs in games such as DayZ or Dark Souls (manageable one-on-one, overwhelming in groups, and easy to die if hit by zombies). 

The intention is that even if you kill all the zombies and clear an area, it won't stay clear until your escape; after a few minutes, the area will be swarming with zombies again. 
This is designed to create a situation where it's essentially futile to try and kill them all. 

It is intended so that in the later stages, humans aren't the only ones left- Zombies will also continue to roam the streets and maintain tension throughout the game.



[h3]Q. I prefer a brute-force style of charging into battles. Is it very difficult to play as such in the early stages of the game?[/h3]
[b]A. [/b]You can do it, but it will cost you. 
If you invest in good armor and weapons and carry them with you, you can engage in this style of play for a while. 
However, it will likely cost more than what you can gain. 
Also, once your armor breaks, you won't be able to go brute force.



[h3]Q. Up to how many people can join in one session?[/h3]
[b]A. [/b]10~16 players would be able to join at random but this is not set in stone. It’s Free for All.



[h3]Q. How many people can be in one squad?[/h3]
[b]A. [/b]We support a maximum of 2 players per squad. 
Beyond that, the game genre would shift towards zombie massacre, so there are no plans for more than 2 players in a squad. 



[h3]Q. Can you obtain rare items from police stations, fire stations, hospitals, military checkpoints, etc. (e.g., military checkpoint, police station = revolver, shotgun, ammunition, taser, baton, military helmet, flak jacket, riot shield, helmet visor, tear gas, smoke grenade / fire station = fire axe, fire extinguisher, fire helmet, fire suit, gas mask / hospital = vaccine sample, antibiotics, painkillers, research lab keycard)?[/h3]
[b]A. [/b]We are trying to place items where you might find them. 
We are doing our best to balance and arrange everything within the given time frame.



[h3]Q. Are cars available for farming?[/h3]
[b]A. [/b]Some cars are available.



[h3]Q. Can we expect locations filled with stories or the stories of other survivors (e.g., the never-gets-old story of a loving father, the situation of becoming stuck in school written and drawn on a wall, etc.)? Personally, I think it would be great if there were hidden items in such places.[/h3]
[b]A. [/b]That definitely sounds like something I would like, but it is too early to add these types of details. 
If the game does well, we may be able to incorporate these kinds of elements in the future.



[h3]Q. Would there be special enemies like cultists, scavengers (hostile survivors), or similar unique adversaries?[/h3]
[b]A. [/b]Currently, there are no plans for NPCs other than zombies. However, the ideas you mentioned have been discussed internally before as well.



[h3]Q. Can you sound the sirens of special vehicles (police cars, fire trucks, ambulances, tow trucks, security vehicles)?[/h3]
[b]A. [/b]Currently, there is no such feature. 



[h3]Q. Will characters be affected by weather and temperature?[/h3]
[b]A. [/b]Currently, there is no such feature, but we are considering adding it if time allows. 
To be precise, we want to introduce various weather conditions and gameplay changes based on them in the future, but there are no development plans at the moment.



[h3]Q. I know the developers would have surely thought this through, but wouldn't a first-person perspective suit the genre better?[/h3]
[b]A. [/b]The debate between first-person and third-person perspectives can likely go on endlessly. 
However, at this point, we thought it would be best if we give a brief answer, as everyone has yet to play the game.
[list]
[*] Confirmation needed: There seemed to be a lively debate about this in the chat on this topic. This was indeed a sharp bone of contention within the development team as well. The conclusion of the debate was that it ultimately depends on ‘what type of game NAKWON is’. So, we decided to quickly develop the game and confirm that our choice was the most fitting.
[*] Perspective shift: We are making this game not as a "kill-others" game but as a "survive-in-chaos" game. These two concepts are quite different. The former provides various ways to kill others, while the latter must offer various ways for players to survive.
[*] Survival suitability: In terms of player interactions, third-person view was more suitable for making various choices (combat, cover, escape, diversion, etc.) actually work. Of course, there are certain players who (quite astonishingly) can do all of this in first-person, but it's challenging for most gamers.
[*] Genre adaptation needed: This genre (farming-escape) itself is not yet a major market and has not been standardized. New genres require new styles of gameplay. When battle royales first started gaining popularity, people had to adapt to playing differently from what they were used to (for example, running away or camping could also lead to victory). Likewise, I believe that this genre we are trying now hasn't been standardized yet, and when people encounter it for the first time, they will need to adapt to playing differently than before. Once everyone adapts to this genre, I think it may become possible for them to play in first-person.
[/list]

In conclusion, we hope everyone will play the game and see if this a good approach.



[h3]Q. What are the minimum / recommended specs of NAKWON?[/h3]
[b]A. [/b]
[Recommended PC Requirements]
[list]
[*] OS: Windows 10 x64 (or higher)
[*] CPU: Intel i7-7700K / AMD Ryzen 5 2600X
[*] RAM: 16 GB
[*] GPU: GeForce RTX 2060 or AMD Radeon RX 5600XT
[*] API:  Direct X 12
[*] Network: High-speed internet connection
[/list]

[Minimum PC Requirements]
[list]
[*] OS: Windows 10 x64
[*] CPU: Intel i5-3570 / AMD FX-8350
[*] RAM: 8 GB
[*] GPU: GeForce GTX 1050Ti or AMD Radeon RX 570
[*] API:  Direct X 12
[*] Network: High-speed internet connection
[/list]

notes.title: About NAKWON: LAST PARADISE
notes.content:
[h2][b]<Overview>[/b][/h2]
NAKWON: LAST PARADISE is a third-person Zombie Apocalypse Stealth Survival game in the backdrop of Seoul. 
A new form of 'Post-Apocalypse Life' that you have yet to experience arises, along with 'Looting Escape'. You gather resources from the PvPvE City, a place where Zombies and Survivors are mixed. The 'Simulation' involves eating, sleeping, paying rent, and earning money to enhance your Citizen Grade within the new societal structure.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44659710/72e0b454ac2dc5261617901b2ad4572f7ecafea7.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44659710/049c62da5cf6ed34607e41de20802d1063f555c6.jpg[/img]
[h2][b]<Genre>[/b][/h2]
NAKWON is a PvPvE game in the genre of Zombie Apocalypse Stealth Survival. 
In this survival game, you have to sneak into the city and collect Resources for your survival.
This game has two major aspects: Scouting and Simulation. 
You have to gather Resources from the city and use those Resources to enhance yourself.
For Scouting, sneak into the outskirts of Seoul, infested by Zombies. Move between buildings, collecting Resources, with the ultimate goal of escaping. You will encounter Zombies (AI) and other Survivors (Players) while needing to figure out your own way to survive and escape.
For Simulation, you make use of what you have collected during Scouting for survival. Survivors have gathered to establish the last city, 'NAKWON,' where they sell Resources and make money.
Money is the means for Survivors to get what they need and get a higher Citizen Grade, granting them to have more privileges and benefits.
Every day, you must decide whether to go out for Scouting or staying inside. But, you must consistently secure more food to avoid starvation and make the best choice whenever an unexpected event occurs.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44659710/52c6b0a4525366e3e74ce2118b8a4de3f2cc1b61.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44659710/adb9f956e7767f9de7731581dc4dc40fd97c24d3.jpg[/img]
[h2][b]<Core Fun>[/b][/h2]
The core fun of this game lies in your ability to survive on your own, amidst the extreme tension with aggressive Zombies and unreliable Survivors. 
Survivors compete for limited resources or find ways to survive without casualties. 
Immerse yourself in a true survival game where powerful Zombies and greedy Humans coexist.

[h2][b]<Features>[/b][/h2]
The unique setting in Seoul will elevate your gaming experience to a level unlike anything you've played before. Here, Zombies behave like humans but are more powerful and will relentlessly pursue you.

[h2][b]▶  Zombie Apocalypse in Seoul[/b][/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44659710/bba4ba35675c46d053417a7f93e2fd3839fc9ead.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44659710/16b7aaf28a270f4460ff304eef651c6c380282cd.jpg[/img]
[h3][b]- Guns are scarce:[/b][/h3]
Due to the law, firearms were prohibited in Korea until the advent of the Zombie Apocalypse.
While some guns were once under the control of the military, the Apocalypse rapidly wrought devastation across the entire world, depleting ammunition stocks almost instantly.
Currently, only a limited number of revolvers and shotguns, used by select policemen and authorized hunters, are available in the market. Notably, consumables like bullets are more expensive than the guns themselves.

[h3][b]- The most ideal city for concealment, closure, and escaping:[/b][/h3]
Seoul ranks seventh in population density, with lots of buildings tightly clustered, and every alley filled with parked cars. 
This city's densely packed elements provide the perfect environment for hiding and escaping from Zombies, which is why it has a high number of Survivors within and around it.

[h3][b]- Where Resources are untouched: [/b][/h3]
Most of the Resources of the country are concentrated in its capital city. 
With the Zombie Apocalypse, the city has been devastated and locked, but it still has a lot of Resources remaining.

[h2][b]▶  Zombies behave like humans but they are more powerful[/b][/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44659710/1cc0a8f35107906e9df32fd63605c0a6df1ea131.jpg[/img]
[h3][b]- Undefeatable Zombies: [/b][/h3]
There is no way you can defeat Zombies, which is why the entire world failed to contain the disaster. 
Unlike the ones you used to see in movies, the best you can do is to disable them just for a brief moment, no matter how, as they will still rise again to attack humans. 
It is still unknown how they revive, and the only officially confirmed fact is that they can repeatedly come back to life without any limits.

[h3][b]- Zombies behave like humans:[/b][/h3]
Just like Humans, zombies use their senses; they react to sounds and rely on their sight to detect and chase after their prey.
Zombies are diurnal creatures, spending their daytime hunting Humans, but mostly sleeping at night.
Do not make any contact or noise to avoid waking them up, as they become active once awakened.

[h2][b]▶  A lawless and chaotic survival game set in a dystopian world[/b][/h2]
[h3][b]- Every man for themselves: [/b][/h3]
Even in the fallen world, you must carry on with your life. 
The objective of scouting is to ensure your safe return. While the fate of the humanity may hang in the balance, your top priority remains your own survival.
This holds true whether you are scouting solo or with a friend; your life always comes first in order to escape.
In this world, your survival is the only thing that matters.

[h3][b]- No one wins, no one loses: [/b][/h3]
Each survivor sets out on a scavenge run. 
Once they obtain what they need for survival in the city, they have to find their own path to escape.
Other survivors' escape has nothing to do with your survival. 
Of course, you will find yourself competing for limited resources and resorting to violence, even murder, to plunder.
You can either aggressively engage to compete for a large sum of money or choose to run away and save your life. 
But remember that avoiding competitions altogether will never be the perfect answer to the ever-increasing cost of living.
You have to build your own strategy for survival.

[h2][b]<Under Development>[/b][/h2]
We began with only a few members in December 2022. 
Development is still in its initial phase, with our current focus on essential components for Scouting. 
There's much work ahead for Simulation.

[h2][b]<Plans Ahead>[/b][/h2]
Even though it's in the initial phases, we are preparing for a pre-alpha test to let everyone experience the unique fun of our game.
Since there are still bugs to fix and improvements to make, we were not sure about showcasing a work-in-progress title. However, to deliver fresh gaming experiences, we decided to share our game with the audience and check out your reactions.
The pre-alpha test is scheduled for 2023, and we will share more details soon. 
Try it for yourself and enjoy this new game development journey with us!
